label: CFR
brief: Council on Foreign Relations, founded New York 1921 from the 1919 Paris peace-conference plan that also produced London's Chatham House; a documented US foreign-policy personnel and consensus network (placement into State, Defense, NSC and intelligence roles).

label: Trilateral Comm.
brief: Trilateral Commission, founded 1973 by David Rockefeller and Zbigniew Brzezinski to coordinate North America, Western Europe and Japan; much of its early US membership staffed the Carter administration (a documented elite-recruitment pipeline).

label: Bilderberg
brief: Annual private conference of about 120-150 political, business and academic figures, founded 1954; held under the Chatham House Rule with no minutes. Its alumni-to-government pipeline is documented; the 'secret world government' framing is unsupported, and the elite-network reading (Domhoff) versus the pluralist reading (Dahl) remains an unsettled academic debate.

label: WEF
brief: World Economic Forum, founded 1971 by Klaus Schwab; promotes 'stakeholder capitalism' and runs Davos and the Young Global Leaders program. The Great Reset is a real 2020 WEF initiative; the 'you'll own nothing' line comes from a 2016 speculative essay by Ida Auken, not WEF policy.

label: Federal Reserve
brief: US central bank, created by the Federal Reserve Act of 1913 after the 1910 Jekyll Island drafting meeting. Regional-Reserve-Bank stock is held only by member banks, is non-transferable and carries no control, with surplus earnings paid to the Treasury; the claim that the Rothschilds or private bankers secretly own the Fed is therefore structurally false.

label: BIS
brief: Bank for International Settlements, Basel, founded 1930 under the Young Plan (WWI reparations); the oldest international financial institution and the hub of central-bank coordination. In March 1939 it honoured an order transferring Czechoslovak gold held at the Bank of England to a Reichsbank account.

Bank of England
brief: Bank of England, founded 1694 to finance war against France; privately owned by stockholders until nationalised by the Attlee government in 1946, after which its capital has been held by HM Treasury. Its hands-off stance enabled the London eurodollar market from the late 1950s.

Fabian Society
brief: British socialist society founded 1884; method of 'permeation' and gradualism (Sidney Webb's 'inevitable gradualness'). Founded the LSE (1895) and helped found the Labour Party (drafted Clause IV, 1918). The 'secret society' framing is contradicted by its open, publishing membership, and historians (McBriar) judge its permeation influence often overstated.

label: Mont Pelerin Society
brief: Neoliberal scholarly society founded 1947 by Friedrich Hayek; intellectual hub of the postwar free-market revival. Funded largely by US foundations (Volker, Earhart) and Swiss banking; the claim that the Bank of England funded it via Baron Grantchester rests on a single secondary source describing 'support', not funding, and the leading history (Slobodian) traces the school to post-Habsburg Vienna, not the British Empire.

label: Round Table movement
brief: Imperial-federalist movement founded 1909 from Lord Milner's circle ('Milner's Kindergarten'); produced the Round Table journal (1910) and helped found Chatham House (1920). Historian Carroll Quigley documented the network in detail but explicitly rejected the 'conspiracy' reading later attached to it.

label: Chatham House (RIIA)
brief: Royal Institute of International Affairs, founded London 1920 from the 30 May 1919 Paris peace-conference plan that also produced the CFR (1921); Britain's pre-eminent foreign-affairs institute and the origin of the Chatham House Rule.

label: Tavistock Institute
brief: Tavistock Institute of Human Relations, London, founded 1947 (Rockefeller-funded, about 30 staff); pioneered action research, socio-technical systems and group relations. The 'global mind-control' conspiracy (John Coleman's Committee of 300) is unsupported and traces to 1970s LaRouche literature.

label: Eugenics Society (UK)
brief: British eugenics body founded as the Eugenics Education Society 1907 (Galton honorary president); renamed the Eugenics Society 1926, the Galton Institute 1989, and the Adelphi Genetics Forum 2021. Postwar it shifted toward population and 'biosocial' fertility work.

label: American Eugenics Society
brief: US eugenics organization founded 1926 (Irving Fisher, Charles Davenport); its journal Eugenics Quarterly was renamed Social Biology in 1969 and the society became the Society for the Study of Social Biology in 1972 as the eugenics label became a liability.

label: Pioneer Fund
brief: US foundation established 1937 by textile heir Wickliffe Draper with Harry Laughlin as first president to fund hereditarian 'race betterment' research; continued financing controversial hereditarian IQ studies into the late 20th century.

label: City of London Corporation
brief: Municipal authority governing the City of London financial district; constitutionally unique (incorporated by prescription; retains a business and livery franchise abolished elsewhere in 1969), with its own police force and the Remembrancer parliamentary-liaison office. Claims that it is a sovereign state-within-a-state, or that the Remembrancer vets legislation, are unsupported.

label: Schiller Institute
brief: International political and cultural organization founded 1984 by Helga Zepp-LaRouche; the main international arm of the LaRouche movement, and since about 2019 a prominent Belt-and-Road advocate. Distinct from the US Promethean Action faction after a 2021 split.

label: Promethean Action
brief: US political organization, the 2024 rebrand of LaRouchePAC; promotes 'American System' economics (Hamilton, Carey, List, Lincoln) and argues that both Keynesian and Austrian economics are British-imperial projects. Split from the Schiller Institute / Zepp-LaRouche wing in 2021.

label: Rothschild & Co
brief: Independent financial-advisory and wealth-management firm descended from the 19th-century Rothschild banking houses that dominated the sovereign-bond market roughly 1820s-1870s; today a mid-tier advisory house. The 'Rothschilds rule the world / own the central banks' narrative is a documented antisemitic conspiracy theory whose Waterloo origin story is an 1846 hoax.

label: Rhodes Trust
brief: Rhodes Trust, established 1902 under Cecil Rhodes's will to fund the Rhodes Scholarships at Oxford; the endowment that bankrolled the Milner / Round Table imperial-federation network.

label: London School of Economics
brief: London School of Economics, founded 1895 by Fabian Society members Sidney and Beatrice Webb to train an administrative and policy class.
